name: Hensoldt AG (HAG.DE, Frankfurt/XETRA, currency EUR)
consensus_source: https://stockanalysis.com/quote/etr/HAG/forecast/ (data S&P Global; cross-checked on marketscreener.com consensus which also shows 15 analysts, average target 92.17 EUR)
upcoming_dates: 2026-11-10 | investor day | Capital Markets Day 2026, London | https://investors.hensoldt.net/financial-calendar/ | primary
product: Sensor solutions and defence electronics: radar (TRML-4D, TRS-4D, Eurofighter Mk1), optronics (Puma, Schakal), electronic attack (Knifefish), avionics for eVTOL, cyber, and CMS330 command systems; repositioning as a software-defined neo-system house.
demand: Surging and policy-driven. European and German defence budget increases drove H1 2026 order intake to double to EUR 2812m and a record backlog of EUR 10356m, with demand from the Bundeswehr and other European states.
pricing_power: Not disclosed and apparently limited: growth and margin gains are volume-driven, and cost-plus style defence procurement constrains visible pricing power; the F126 episode shows programme-level risk.
competition: Intense European and global rivalry: Thales, Leonardo, Rheinmetall, Saab, Elbit Systems, L3Harris, Indra and US primes. HENSOLDT is a niche sensor, optronics and electronic-warfare leader listed in MDAX and TecDAX.
team: Management Board: Oliver Doerre (CEO), Christian Ladurner (CFO), Inka Tews (CHRO); Supervisory Board chaired by Reiner Winkler. Insider buying: Doerre acquired shares 2026-06-22 and 2026-06-26, Tews 2026-06-23 and 2026-06-24.
market_strategy: Shift from traditional sensor supplier to neo-system house systems integrator: networked, software-defined defence and AI sensor fusion; expand manufacturing and logistics capacity, integrate the Nedinsco optronics acquisition, and open a Stuttgart Software-Defined Defence centre (2026-08-04).
bull: H1 2026 primary results (2026-07-31): order intake doubled to EUR 2812m, record backlog EUR 10356m, revenue +23.6%, adjusted EBITDA +28.5%, FY26 outlook confirmed; insiders Doerre and Tews bought shares in June 2026.
bear: H1 adjusted FCF negative EUR -136m; FY26 margin 18.5-19.0% vs H1 11.8% needs heavy H2; F126 cancelled 2026-06-30 (over EUR 200m); ~40x forward P/E; Jefferies cut to Hold 2026-08-05.
falsifier: The 2026-11-05 9M 2026 statement shows FY26 revenue below about EUR 2750m or adjusted EBITDA margin below 18.5%, or free cash flow still negative.
web_what_changed: H1 2026 results 2026-07-31 primary: order intake doubled to EUR 2812m, record backlog EUR 10356m, revenue EUR 1167m up 23.6 percent, adjusted EBITDA EUR 137m up 28.5 percent, FY26 outlook confirmed (revenue about EUR 2750m, book-to-bill 1.5-2.0x, margin 18.5-19.0 percent). 2026-06-30 F126 frigate programme terminated; 2026-06-01 free cash flow guidance raised.
web_not_known_yesterday: No new company-specific filing found. Market context (aggregator): on 2026-09-24 Hensoldt closed down 3.1 percent at EUR 76.38 in a broad European defence selloff (Rheinmetall, RENK) tied to geopolitical headlines including a G20 invitation to Putin; shares sit about 35 percent below the 52-week peak.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and demand led, not price. H1 2026 revenue rose 23.6 percent on higher core-business volumes from rising European defence spending; Optronics revenue up 63.2 percent, Sensors up 16.9 percent. Mix is shifting toward optronics and software-defined, with some pass-through revenue in Eurofighter Mk1 radar and PEGASUS.
web_suppliers: Not itemised by the company (not found). Implied dependencies: electronic and semiconductor and RF components, subcontractors and skilled labour. HENSOLDT is expanding capacity and recruiting about 300 staff (2026-08-04, Bosch cooperation, Stuttgart), indicating skilled labour is a binding constraint. Thales Netherlands is the F126 prime partner, relationship unsettled after the 2026-06-30 termination.
web_customers: Highly concentrated on governments. H1 2026 order intake came from the Federal Republic of Germany (BAAINBw/Bundeswehr) and other European states; the German state holds about 25.1 percent of shares, Leonardo about 22.8 percent. Named programmes: Eurofighter Mk1 radar, PEGASUS, Puma, Schakal, TRML-4D; exports to Brazil and India. Exact percentage concentration not found.
web_who_loses: Competing sensor, radar and defence-electronics primes: Thales (France), Leonardo, Rheinmetall (also a partner), Saab, Elbit, L3Harris, Indra, plus US primes bidding for European programmes. F126 naval suppliers lose, while MEKO-class builders may gain from German Navy re-procurement.
web_contradicting_evidence: Germany cancelled the F126 frigate programme on 2026-06-30 (HENSOLDT share just over EUR 200m). H1 2026 adjusted free cash flow stayed negative at EUR -136m. FY26 margin guidance 18.5-19.0 percent versus H1 11.8 percent implies heavy H2 and Q4 execution risk. Valuation is about 40x forward P/E, shares about 35 percent below peak, and Jefferies cut to Hold 2026-08-05.
web_if_management_right: Meeting FY26 guidance means revenue about EUR 2750m, book-to-bill 1.5-2.0x sustaining the over EUR 10bn backlog, adjusted EBITDA margin 18.5-19.0 percent, cash conversion about 50 percent and net leverage about 1.5x; consensus sees 2027 revenue about EUR 3234m (IR consensus 2026-06-06), supporting the EUR 92.17 mean target, about 22 percent above EUR 75.7.
web_if_management_wrong: First to break is H2 and Q4 revenue and margin conversion, since deliveries and acceptances are back-half loaded; a miss would compress the adjusted EBITDA margin and cash conversion, threaten the about 1.5x leverage target, and de-rate a roughly 40x forward P/E while questioning the quality of the EUR 10.36bn backlog.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Rheinmetall (air-defence integration via Skynex and Skymaster, 2026-08-19); Bosch and the Baden-Wuerttemberg region (staff and property, 2026-08-04); MEKO and other shipyards if German Navy re-procurement proceeds; upstream RF and semiconductor, test-equipment and subcontractor firms, plus German small and mid-cap defence electronics.
